mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement provides an explicit integer count for an individual.
mathgap.example: A statement says "Alice has 12 oranges" but the solver treats it as a later or partial count instead of setting Alice = 12 immediately.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more items than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer items than Y" as X = Y - N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses "more" or "fewer" to compare two quantities.
mathgap.example: Misreading "Bob has 3 fewer apples than Carol" as Bob = Carol + 3 instead of Bob = Carol - 3.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, give each recipient half of the original amount and set the giver's count to zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a split‑all operation.
mathgap.example: Treating "Sam splits all his oranges between Tom and Sue" as Sam keeps his oranges instead of giving them away.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, and use these updated counts for any later statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a "gives" or "transfers" statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: Using the giver's original count after a transfer instead of the reduced count in a subsequent equation.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference on one side of an equality is already known, substitute its numeric value into the equation to simplify and solve for unknowns.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When an equality of signed differences contains a difference whose value has been determined elsewhere.
mathgap.example: Failing to replace a known (A‑B)=5 in the equation (A‑B)=(C‑D), leaving the system under‑determined.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Process the statements in the order given, updating counts after each step; later statements refer to the updated counts, not the initial ones.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any problem where statements can affect each other's values, especially with transfers.
mathgap.example: Using a person's pre‑transfer count in a statement that appears after the transfer.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: When a conditional transfer statement appears (e.g., "If X has more than N items, X will transfer t items to Y"), first check the condition using the current count, then apply the transfer only if the condition holds.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer is guarded by a condition.
mathgap.example: Applying a transfer even though the giver does not satisfy the "more than" condition.

mathgap.title: Target variable dependency analysis
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal set of equations needed to solve for the target variable by tracing dependencies from the target back through the statements, ignoring unrelated chains.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains many statements, most of which are irrelevant to the queried person.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations instead of focusing on the subset that influences the target variable.

mathgap.title: Signed difference handling with trivial equality detection
mathgap.principle: When a statement involves a signed difference, interpret "difference between X and Y" as the signed difference X − Y, preserve the order of terms, translate equalities as (A − B) = (C − D), and if both sides are syntactically identical, discard the statement as it provides no new information.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement contains a signed difference or an equality of signed differences.
mathgap.example: The statement "The number of oranges that James has more than Myles is equal to the difference between the number of oranges that James and Myles have" is a trivial equality and should be ignored.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses "difference between X and Y" with an unsigned distance and may reverse the subtraction order, leading to sign errors.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always treat "difference between X and Y" as the signed expression X − Y and keep the order exactly as written.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model updates counts only after processing all statements, forgetting that earlier transfers affect later references.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, updating both giver and receiver before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a given count as the final value, overlooking later transfers that modify it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as the current value at that point; later transfer statements may change it.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers unconditionally, missing the prerequisite condition.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Check the condition using the current count before applying a conditional transfer.

mathgap.description: Failing to recognize trivial signed difference equalities (identical expressions on both sides) and treating them as informative
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model parses the statement literally and assumes it adds a new constraint, leading to wasted effort or contradictory equations.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Detect when both sides of a signed‑difference equality are the same expression; discard such statements as they provide no new information.
